articles.title: Hackers Used Meta’s AI Support Bot to Seize Instagram Accounts
articles.summary: Microsoft just served up a record-breaking 200 security holes in one Patch Tuesday, including 36 critical bugs. Even for a company that treats vulnerabilities like a subscription service, this is impressively broken.

articles.title: LGBT Q&A: We’re Back With Season 2!
articles.summary: CISA contractor accidentally published AWS GovCloud keys and agency secrets on GitHub because apparently even cybersecurity agencies can't handle basic operational security. Congress is now asking the obvious questions everyone else was already screaming.

articles.title: Enshittification Merch That Actually Fights Enshittification
articles.summary: Section 702 mass surveillance authority faces its final countdown as Congress finally considers requiring warrants for spying on Americans. About time someone remembered the Fourth Amendment exists.

articles.title: Scott Pelley Shows How Legacy Media Got It Wrong — Before Bari Weiss Made It Worse
articles.summary: Nightmare-Eclipse drops another Windows zero-day called RoguePlanet, continuing their beautiful revenge arc against Microsoft. When responsible disclosure fails, public embarrassment is the next best teacher.

articles.title: Top Pentagon Official Admits Boat Strike May Have Killed Victims of Human Trafficking
articles.summary: Bipartisan momentum builds to rein in domestic spying laws with unprecedented support. Sen. Wyden says he's never seen this level of cooperation, which means the surveillance state must be really pissing people off.

articles.title: Chinese agents caught rebuilding botnets and stirring the pot on AI datacenter debate
articles.summary: Some CEO stored every employee password in a single Excel file to 'solve email issues.' This is why we can't have nice things and also why security researchers develop drinking problems.

articles.title: GitHub pulls pin on npm's auto-run scripts
articles.summary: Angry researcher with Microsoft beef drops fresh Windows zero-day because revenge is indeed a dish best served as weaponized code. The vulnerability disclosure process is working exactly as intended, obviously.

articles.title: Lack of White House guidance has complicated agency Mythos adoption, people familiar say
articles.summary: GitHub finally disables npm install scripts by default to stop supply chain attacks. Only took them until malware was auto-executing on every package install, but hey, better late than never.

articles.title: France’s ‘sovereign’ messenger Tchap was breached, and officials and the hacker disagree on how badly
articles.summary: France's 'sovereign' government messaging platform Tchap got breached through basic account hijacking. Building your own encrypted messenger to avoid trusting WhatsApp, then getting owned anyway, is peak irony.

articles.title: New Windows Zero-Day Exploit ‘RoguePlanet’ Released
articles.summary: Critical Ivanti Sentry flaws allow root-level remote code execution with perfect 10.0 and 9.9 CVSS scores. When your security appliance becomes the attack vector, someone's having a very bad day.
